title: No agreement exists in the record between the water district and the campus it is building for
detail: The Adams County Regional Water District designed, bid and permitted a water main to serve the Buck Canyon site, and its own minutes commit it to 100,000 gallons per day of potable and "supplemental cooling water" on an interim basis. The corpus holds the District's engineering (the Ginger Ridge plan set), its confidentiality obligation (the executed 2024-01-10 NDA) and thirty months of board minutes — and NOT the contract. There is no service agreement, no cost-participation or reimbursement agreement, no capacity reservation and no tap agreement anywhere in the record, and the District's own 2024 and 2025 capital budgets carry no Ginger Ridge line item. That is consistent with a customer-funded project outside the appropriation, but the agreement is what would establish who pays, what capacity is reserved, and on what terms a public utility committed it. R.C. 149.43 request to ACRWD is the route.
note: OWED RECORD — the single largest gap in this site's assembly record.

title: The court entry that created the water district is cited in its by-laws but not held
detail: The District's 1994 by-laws recite that its Board of Trustees "shall be composed as per the Entry of the Court for the District, as filed with the Clerk of the Court of Common Pleas of Adams County, Ohio, on January 10, 1994 under Case No. 930355". That entry is the District's creating instrument under R.C. Ch. 6119 and it fixes how the nine trustees are composed — the question the 1997-98 self-appointment resolutions raise and cannot answer. ⚠️ ROUTE IS NOT SCRIPTABLE. The Adams County Clerk of Courts record search (adamscountycourts.com/recordSearch.php) is gated by Google reCAPTCHA, which is an access control and was not circumvented; a 1993-filed case is also likely to predate the online index. Pull in person or by mail from the Clerk of Courts, 110 West Main Street, West Union, OH 45693, (937) 544-2344.
note: OWED RECORD — cited by a committed instrument, absent from the corpus.

title: Ohio EPA's plan approval for the Ginger Ridge water main was days away and is not held
detail: At the meeting of 2026-07-09 the District's engineer reported that Ohio EPA "review was complete and they should be getting the approval letter sent by the following week" — i.e. on or about 2026-07-13. The approval letter and its conditions are not in the corpus, and its issuance is unconfirmed. The approved capacity it states is the one document that would put a number on what this main is permitted to deliver, against the 100,000 gpd the minutes commit. ⚠️ NO PUBLIC SEARCH SURFACED. Ohio EPA's DDAGW engineering/plan-approval pages 404 and the ePlan submission platform is authenticated. Route is a records request to DDAGW (DDAGW.Engineering@epa.ohio.gov) or to the District. The system key for any such request is now established — see ACRWD-PWSID below.
note: OWED RECORD — time-sensitive; the letter should exist as of 2026-07.

title: The District's public water system ID is OH0100012, and the system is groundwater-sourced
detail: Established 2026-08-16 from Ohio EPA's own 2026 Adams County monitoring schedule — "OH0100012 ADAMS COUNTY REGIONAL WD PWS, System Type Community, Source Ground Water", sampling facility 152614, entry point EP001, distribution DS1/DS000, and a Ground Water Rule "Substantial System" designation. This is [verified] and it is the key any Ohio EPA drinking-water records request needs. ⚠️ Do NOT confuse it with OH0100112, which is Manchester Village's WTP — a different Adams County system, and Manchester is the mailing town of the Buck Canyon site. The groundwater source corroborates the minutes' repeated "new wells" language for the larger supply project, and makes aquifer capacity, not river withdrawal, the question for this site.
source: Ohio EPA 2026 PWS Monitoring Schedules, Adams County (data/documents/oepa/west-union/Adams.pdf, PDF pp. 4-6) · data/extracted/oepa/west-union/OH0100012.pws-schedule.yaml
note: Captured 2026-10-28 (#2137) and transcribed as an extraction, not a data/reference artifact, since no watermark subcommand regenerates it. The page cite was "pp. 3-4" until then; the OH0100012 schedule is on PDF pages 4-6. The epa.ohio.gov/Portals/28 path first cited now returns 404; the dam.assets.ohio.gov mirror serves the file.

title: Roughly half the board minutes covering the project period were not produced
detail: The District meets monthly (2nd Thursday, per its Code of By-Laws Article I). The corpus holds 15 of the roughly 31 meetings between 2024-01 and 2026-07. Absent are all of February-September and November-December 2024, and January-March, June and August-September 2025. The two 2024 minutes that WERE produced are precisely the two carrying the project's origin (the NDA authorization and the first "Project Galaxy" naming), which is consistent with a responsive production rather than a full series pull — but the request that produced this set is not in the corpus either, so the scope cannot be checked against what was asked for.
note: OWED RECORD — request the full minute book 2023-2026, plus the original request and response.

title: How the sitting board was appointed is undocumented between 1999 and 2026
detail: The committed governance file stops in 1998. It shows a board that fills its own vacancies through a nominating committee, with the trustees being re-appointed abstaining on their own re-appointments (Res. 97-119, 98-90). Four members of the board that authorized the Buck Canyon NDA had held their seats since at least 1997-98 — Tony Staggs, Gerald Gray, Chris Baxla and Daniel Fristoe — and no appointment record for the intervening twenty-five years is in the corpus. Whether the Common Pleas court retained any role in composition after the 1994 entry is also unresolved and turns on ACRWD-COURT-ENTRY-930355.
note: OWED RECORD — R.C. 149.43 request for all trustee appointment resolutions 1999-2026.

title: Five substantial Ohio EPA documents are shelved and unread
detail: The 2026-08-17 eDoc pull brought in 32 Buck Canyon documents; one is extracted and five big ones are held, hashed and unread beyond page 1. The 554-page JURISDICTIONAL WATERS DELINEATION REPORT (edoc-3940065) is the document the USACE email production named and omitted. The 196-page SWP3 (edoc-4147395) is the most detailed engineering description of the site in the corpus and should carry grading limits, drainage areas and outfalls. Ramboll's 37-page technical response (edoc-4003954) is the review round that produced the permit. The mitigation plan (edoc-3940079) and seven ORAM v5.0 wetland scoring forms round it out. Also unfinished within the extracted permit itself: pages 3-8 of 9, which hold the mitigation terms and the Part IV notification schedule.
note: Not a retrieval gap — a reading gap. Everything named here is already in the corpus.

title: Ohio EPA serves one document of this file truncated at exactly 2 MiB
detail: edoc-3940059.pdf arrives at exactly 2,097,152 bytes with the server's own Content-Length agreeing on all three attempts — a valid %PDF-1.7 header, no %%EOF, and refused by both pypdf and pdfium. The truncation is on Ohio EPA's side, not in transit. The bytes are retained under chain of custody as evidence of the defect, but the document's content is unknown and nothing may be cited from it. Routes: ask Ohio EPA DSW for a re-serve or a copy by R.C. 149.43, or check whether the same exhibit appears intact elsewhere in the 25-document application package.
note: Worth reporting to Ohio EPA regardless of this project — a portal that silently serves 2 MiB of a larger file is a general integrity problem for anyone relying on that route.

title: Four instruments, two entity families, and nothing joins them
detail: 68 YARDS, LLC — principal Carrie Tillman, of Chicago, Illinois — holds the USACE NWP 39 verification and the Ohio Level Two Isolated Wetland Permit. BUCK CANYON PROPERTIES, LLC / BUCK CANYON LLC — Derek Harmon, of Flemingsburg, Kentucky — holds the USACE jurisdictional determination, the NPDES construction stormwater coverage, and county parcel 1830000070002. One project, four instruments, two entity families, and NO document in the corpus connects them. Ohio SOS is retrieval-blocked; ILLINOIS (68 Yards' stated domicile) and Delaware registries are untried and are the obvious next route. (Street addresses and contact emails are deliberately not repeated in this derived lead — they are on the instruments themselves and in the collections' filename-maps, which is where they belong. The names, places and instrument assignments are the whole analytic point.)
note: OWED RECORD — this is the site's central unresolved entity question.

title: The campus parcel's owner is named by a survey, and the deed is still not held
detail: The campus is Adams County parcel 1830000079000, Sprigg Township, deeded 1016.2174 ac. This was established 2026-08-16 by point-in-polygon against the coordinate the USACE itself published (38.646748 / -83.659828), and it matches the "approximately 1,016 acres" in the federal project description. The geometry is committed at data/reference/west-union/parcel-assemblage.geojson. The county's tax-map layer has no CAMA join, so its nulls mean "not served", NOT "unowned". NARROWED 2026-11-03 — the ALTA survey in the County's draft development agreement (Exhibit A, p. 29) labels the parcel "BUCK CANYON PROPERTIES LLC, A KENTUCKY LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY / VOL. 636 PAGE 182 / INST. NO. 2024-912". That is the survey's statement, not the deed. The deed would give the grantor, the conveyance date and the consideration, and it is still not held. ⚠️ The same draft's §8.14 and Exhibit I call Amazon Data Services, Inc. the site's "owner" / "record owner". That conflict stays open until the recorder answers it. Route: the Adams County Recorder, Inst. 2024-912 (Vol. 636 Pg. 182), plus the Auditor's CAMA record and transfer history for parcel 183-00-00-079.000.
note: OWED RECORD — the conveyance would date the land acquisition. The survey's field date (2021-07-02) is now the earliest dated step in this project's timeline, ahead of the NDAs of 2024-01-04 and 2024-01-10.

title: The 1,016 acres were assembled from at least seven tracts, and nobody has traced who did it
detail: The survey's legal description (County draft agreement, Exhibit A) builds the 1016.2174-ac campus from five whole tracts (194-00-00-006.000, 194-00-00-005.000, 183-00-00-079.000, 183-00-00-079.001, 183-00-00-078.000), 22.214 ac of a 100.722-ac tract (183-00-00-070.000), and part of a 945.997-ac tract (193-00-00-016.000) owned by Hamerkop Development, LLC, O.R. 544 Pg. 694. Roughly 673 ac of it is Hamerkop land (an inference: the total less the fixed parts). The field survey was done 2021-07-02, more than two years before either NDA. This retires the earlier reading of the county tax map as "one tract, no assembly". Who bought each tract, from whom, and when, is open. So is whether Hamerkop Development is related to Buck Canyon. Route: the Adams County Recorder and Auditor transfer history for all seven PIDs, plus O.R. 544 Pg. 694; the Kentucky and Ohio SOS registries for Hamerkop Development, LLC.
note: OWED RECORD — the land roll-up is the step every other site's story starts from.

title: The County posted a draft agreement with Amazon, and no vote or signed copy is held
detail: Adams County's website carries a 123-page DRAFT development agreement with Amazon Data Services, Inc. (PDF built 2026-10-30). The Effective Date, the authorizing "Resolution ___ dated ___" and every signature block are blank, and §8.18 says the County's authorization is given "in a meeting open to the public". Not held: the Commissioners' resolution, the journal entry or minutes of that meeting, and any executed copy. The County page that links the PDF was not found either (the download category returns 404), so the posting date and agenda are unknown. ⚠️ §5.6 vests the project against County rules adopted after the Effective Date, so the date of execution decides which rules apply.
note: OWED RECORD — R.C. 149.43 to the Board of Commissioners for the resolution, the journal and the executed agreement. The draft's §8.18 gives the Developer five business days' notice first.

title: An Economic Development Authority NDA predates the Water District's by six days
detail: The County draft agreement recites "That certain Nondisclosure Agreement, dated January 4, 2024, executed by Adams County Economic Development Authority". The Water District's NDA (held) is dated 2024-01-10. The ACEDA instrument, its counterparty, and any ACEDA minutes authorizing it are not held.
note: OWED RECORD — R.C. 149.43 to the Adams County Economic Development Authority.

title: The incentive is a County CRA traded for a JEDD, and neither instrument is held
detail: Draft §8.14 grants a County Community Reinvestment Area exemption (R.C. 3735.65-3735.70). In return, the Developer petitions (Exhibit I) to add the site to a Joint Economic Development District among Sprigg Township, the County and the Village of Manchester, so that the JEDD income tax applies (R.C. 715.72). §8.15 makes every Developer obligation contingent on incentives "acceptable to Developer". Not held: the CRA resolution and agreement (term, percentage), the JEDD contract, Sprigg Township's amending resolution, and any school-board notice or compensation agreement.
note: OWED RECORD — County, Sprigg Township and Village of Manchester records.

title: ODOT approved a "Project Galaxy" traffic study for this campus, and it is not attached
detail: The Kimley-Horn memo of 2026-10-08, written on behalf of AWS and appended to the County draft agreement, cites "the Project Galaxy Traffic Impact Study, approved by the Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) on July 24, 2026 (attached)". The study is not in the PDF. It would carry the trip generation, and so the workforce and phasing, for what the memo calls a "multi-campus data center build-out", Q1 2026 through Q4 2034. It is also the first State record to use the Galaxy codename at this site.
note: OWED RECORD — ODOT District 9 public-records request for the TIS and its approval letter.

title: The County, not Amazon, is set up to be the campus's wastewater permittee
detail: Exhibit H of the County draft agreement has the Developer design and build a water and wastewater treatment facility for the project, with the COUNTY acting "as the governmental applicant or owner" in any PTI or NPDES application, and then owning and operating it under a cost-recovery service agreement. If executed, the campus discharge would be permitted to Adams County. An ECHO or eDocument watch keyed on an Amazon or Buck Canyon permittee name would miss it.
note: Watch the Ohio EPA eDocument portal for an Adams County PTI/NPDES application in Sprigg Township.

title: Every attachment to the federal §404 file is named in the emails and none was produced
detail: The 14 USACE threads are covering messages only. Named and absent are the AJD/PJD letter and its JD Review Area enclosure, the Jurisdictional WOTUS delineation report, the PCN application, BOTH NWP 39 verification letters (2026-02-17 and the 2026-02-18 revision), the Buck Canyon Cemetery Avoidance Plan, the Goodwin Phase I/II archaeology reports, the signed USFWS SLOPES form, the Ohio SHPO review letters (2025ADA66354_1112049 and 2025ADA6635_1112658and1112718), and the USFWS and ODNR tree-clearing concurrence letters. The verification letters matter most — they carry the special conditions the project is actually bound by, including the Condition 7 that was revised within 22 hours of the applicant objecting to it. ⚠️ The production route for the emails themselves is also unestablished — no cover letter, request number or FOIA determination accompanied them, so they must not be cited as "FOIA-released" until the request record is in hand.
note: OWED RECORD — FOIA to USACE Huntington District, Regulatory Division.
